messages:
elaine: quick sync — I ran a mini onboard for raven-14b-quant with a 2-hop speculative handoff (we're calling it 'two-hop' in the bench). small cohort (500 chats) focused on conversational completion workloads.

elaine: tl;dr: p95 latency drops ~25-30% on average, median down ~15%, but we see a ~0.4–0.9% top-1 accuracy regression on long completions (>200 tokens). behavior details below.

raj: nice. what was the fallback policy for mismatched kv states?

elaine: raj: fallback = immediate single-hop decode + cache invalidate for that request. no rollbacks. we logged mismatch_count per request; mismatch ~= 1.2% of requests in cohort.

ben: can you paste the quick numbers? even roughs help.

elaine: sure — quick paste from the run: 
```
model: raven-14b-q
config: twohop, branch_prefill=0.12, speculative_window=8
cohort: 500 convs (avg len 180 tokens)
baseline (no spec): median=28ms, p95=68ms, top1=0.835
two-hop: median=24ms, p95=48ms, top1=0.828
mismatch_rate=1.2% (mismatches where speculative token != final token)
regressions concentrated on long-turn single-token surprisals (tokens 120+)
```

sasha: 0.7% drop on top1 is annoying but still within a tolerable band for some customers. did you check BLEU/ROUGE or just top1?

elaine: we tracked top1 and a small ngram overlap metric — rougeL dropped 0.2 absolute on long completions. for short completions (<50 tokens) quality is indistinguishable.

raj: interesting. could be priority to detect long-turns and disable two-hop early. any cheap heuristic?

elaine: yeah — session_token_count > 120 OR prompt_has_code_block = true -> disable two-hop. that cut mismatches in a follow-up run to 0.4% and recovered ~0.15% top1.

ben: what about cost delta? GPU cycles or token cost?

elaine: cost: runtime GPU-seconds per 1k requests dropped ~18% in two-hop baseline, after heuristic it was ~12% savings (because we disable on the tail). win depends on traffic shape.

deploy-bot: deploy started: branch twohop-experiment -> staging (elaine)

raj: did you try quant parity variants (nf4 vs int4) effects?

elaine: ran both nf4 and int4 quick checks. int4 + twohop had slightly higher mismatch (1.8%) vs nf4 (1.2%) — guessing quant noise amplifies speculative mismatch. quality delta slightly larger for int4. recommending nf4 for two-hop for now.

sasha: good call. next steps?

elaine: propose: 1) expand to 5k convs with rollout heuristics enabled, 2) instrument per-route metrics (mismatch rate, revert rate, latency benefit), 3) add a small safety gate: if mismatch_rate > 1% over 10m, auto-disable two-hop on that route.

ben: +1 to the safety gate. also add a prompt-level signal export so app teams can opt out via header.

elaine: noted — I'll open a brief PR with the rollout plan and metric dashboard spec. aiming to run the 5k expansion tomorrow.

sasha: thanks, elaine. ping me when you have the dashboard link, want to run a quick qual pass on a handful of failing long-turn examples.

elaine: will do. attaching one failing example inline: 
```
prompt: "Write a long-form technical design for a feature that..."
baseline completion (gold): "...performant KV cache with per-shard eviction..."
twohop speculative token sequence started diverging at token 134 and preferred a shorter phrasing, causing a downstream drift in specificity.
```

elaine: not a blocker for internal beta but worth tracking. closing notes: two-hop gives meaningful latency wins on median/p95 for interactive loads, cost wins moderate, quality tradeoffs concentrated on long-turn semantics and amplified by lower-precision quant. rollout with heuristics + safety gate looks viable.

ben: solid. thanks for the quick experiment and writeup.
